si.t: “With proper preparations, the fighting is merely a formality.”

The Scout is an archer-based class that can act early and effectively. He uses preliminary actions to take control of the battlefield, attacks enemies at full health, and quickens himself readily. He is hard to destroy before his turn.

r.t: Scouts are an essential part of enemy army, as only with knowledge of the enemy can success be found. The scouts prepare the battlefield to best support their army’s success.
The scout is lightly armored because he is constantly on the move.

The Scout can implement scouted abilities. These abilities, which come in all three strengths, can only be used as the first action of battle, after which they turn into a related, but lesser, ability.

Bane Targeting – The modified skill has a chance to target all enemies of the same type.

Unerring Marks – After the Marksman attacks a target, all attacks against the target are unerring for a number of times.
Flying Falcon – Falcon can only be targeted by ranged attacks and has increased dodge.
Shared Bounty – Bounty abilities affect the entire team when they trigger.
Tempered Resolve — Whenever the Initiate resists a percentage damage or death effect, his next attack gains increased damage.
Impact Power – The Pugilist deals increased damage if he struck the same target the turn before.
Stunning Roars — Any enemy that is stunned at the beginning of the Skirmisher's turn has their stun duration extended based on level.
Diamond Body — If the Vajra does not target an enemy during his turn, he has a chance to ignore all damage until his next turn.
Pressure Crack — When the Stone Fist scores a critical hit, it also triggers any glancing hit effects on that attack.
Exposed Momentum — Whenever the Infiltrator loses hidden, he is quickened.
Poisonous Refreshment – Whenever the associated proc triggers, the Viper Fang gains a poison use.
Condition Fortress — The Ascetic gains increased affliction resistance for each condition currently affecting him, whether affliction or enchantment.
Thunder Strikes — Whenever the Thunderfist attacks a stunned enemy, that enemy also takes air damage.
Counter from the Ground – The Drunken Master can counter even if prone or disarmed. Higher levels increase chance to counter.
Extended Ambush – Ambush abilities can be used while target has over a percentage of life.
Stacking Bleed Proc – The modified skill has a chance to afflict the target with a stacking bleed.
Trap Disarmament – Whenever the Burglar would otherwise trigger a trap on the field, they have a chance to remove that trap completely.
Grand Larceny — Steal abilities have a chance to trigger a free attack (uses tag system)
Glancing Dodge – Whenever the Acrobat suffers a glancing hit, it has a chance to be considered a dodge based on this skill.
Transfer Contract — Next attack after a contract ends applies that contract to the new target
Double Down — Enemies have a chance not to lose flanked at the start of their turn
Smuggled Poisons - The first poison gained by the smuggler is also shared with all allies. The amount of uses is based on this skill.
Aversion Backstab – Whenever an enemy averted by the skulk attacks, the skulk attacks it in response.
Second Poison — The Ninja can apply a second poison simultaneously
Premade Reserves – Premade abilities have a chance to have multiple uses at the beginning of battle.
True Chaos – Chaos abilities both use a random elemental power and target a random elemental resistance.
Quick Call – Called shots can be activated the same turn they are used.
Ignore Consequences – Whenever the brute would suffer consequences at the beginning of her turn due to a consequences ability, she has a chance to ignore those consequences.
Reckless Attack – Attacks from the Raider have a chance to deal increased damage at the cost of preventing any active defenses until next turn.
Double Exertion – Exertion effects trigger twice.
Initial Rampage – The Marauder begins battle with a value of rampage based on this skill.
Close to the Edge – Attacks the Rager make generate more threshold towards her Brink abilities
Bloody Berserk – Attack the Rager makes while berserk also have backbiting based on the level of this skill.
Vampiric Devotion – Life drain effects are not affected by vitality, but healing has a greater drain on vitality.
Reactive Beast Form – The Beastlord has a chance to gain a beast form whenever damaged.
Massive Power – The threshold for triggering massive damage is lowered for the Destroyer.
High Stakes – Whenever the Gladiator attacks, he has a chance to deal 150% damage or 75% damage, as determined by skill level.
Disarming Follow Up – The Duelist makes an immediate attack against any enemy that gains the disarmed condition.
Hurry Phalanx – Whenever the Phalanx becomes ready, she quickens any ally within a short timer of action threshold to also become ready.
Constant Momentum – If the Dervish begins her turn under a momentum threshold, she generates momentum but is delayed by a greater amount.
Reactive Quickness — whenever the unit uses an ability with the reaction tag, they gain a minor quicken.
Brace for Charge — the unit gains a defense bonus against each incoming attack scaled to the attacker's current momentum.
Battle Hardened — whenever the unit takes damage during its own turn from combat exchanges such as Bushido, counters, or retaliation, it gains enhanced dodge until its next turn.
Growing Defenses - Each attack against Dreadnaught enhances defense until end of her turn.
Responsive Parries – Whenever the Swashbuckler parries an attack, she also makes a counter attack. She has a reduced chance to make counter attacks without parrying though.
Field Commander — Aid abilities used by the unit have enhanced effects and last two turns instead of one.
Protected Intercessions – Whenever the Bodyguard would take damage for an ally, the amount of damage received is reduced by this skill level.
Constant Ire – Attacks from the Champion that deal overkill damage have a multiplier to the overkill value based on this passive.

My Kingdom for a Horse - The Cavalier has a chance to be treated as mounted at the beginning of all turns.
Initial Corruption - The Black Knight begins battle with a certain amount of corruption.
Rainbow Spectrum – The Mercenary deals increased damage for each element she has used during her turn.
Swelling Enchantments – Until the first action of a unit after a Minstrel enchants them, the enchantment has an increased effect, based on this skill level.
Pratfalls – Whenever the Jester becomes prone, he quickens all allies. Whenever the Jester becomes disarmed, he deals ranged damage to a random enemy. Both are based on this skill level.

Mortal Harvest — Whenever the Dirge Singer kills an enemy with an instant kill effect (culling, ruthless, massive damage, or similar), he restores a percentage of his maximum health and a percentage of his maximum mana.

Extended Cuts — Whenever the Balladeer applies a condition that already exists on the target, the maximum duration of that condition is increased. This effect can apply multiple times to the same condition.

Dedicated Entourage — Whenever the Diva grants a provoke to an ally, that provoke lasts for one additional instance.
Encore — When the Muse is killed, he is granted one free resurrection on himself.
Constant Light – No units can gain hidden in battle.
Death Throes – When a companion of the Conjurer would die, it makes one last attack.
Initial Retaliation – The Occultist deals additional damage the first-time retaliation triggers each time she gains it.
Critical Attendance – Whenever the Shaman scores a critical hit, her companion has an increased chance to critical during its turn.
Dualistic Power – Whenever the Medium increases one elemental power or resistance, she increases the opposed power by a percentage of that amount.
Animated Persistence – Animation abilities from the Animist have a chance not to be consumed when they trigger.
Endangered Awakening – Whenever the Spiritualist becomes endangered, she quickens and gains enhanced magic power with her next turn.
Sea of Stars – Whenever the Astrologer scores enough critical hits, she triggers a light magic attack against all enemies.
Dark Harvest – Whenever a unit with corruption on it dies, the Vizier restores mana based on the level of corruption.

Assisted Overheals – Overheals from the Acolyte include a percentage of all health restored, based on the level of this skill.
Reactive Resistance – The Disciple gains elemental resistance based on the last element that damaged him.
Conserve Vitality - The Combat Medic has a chance to keep vitality buffs when damaged based on this passive.
Exorcism – Attacks against intangible enemies have a chance to automatically kill them based on their low health and mana.
Plague Bearer - The Plague Doctor begins battle with contagion that has a chance to spread afflictions to enemies instead.
Enhanced Potential – Whenever the Buccaneer uses an ability that is based on the value of a damage affliction, the value is considered greater, based on this skill level.
Critical Execution – The Executioner deals increased critical damage if the target has the lowest health.
Burial Proc – The modified skill has a chance to afflict the target with burial.
Constant Moon – Moon automatically appears in battle, determined by game calendar, at a lesser power.
Sinful Vapors - The Sin Eater gains mana whenever any affliction is purged.
Nightmare Manifest – Whenever incapacitated is removed from the Sandman, he deals illusory damage to all enemies based on the period he was incapacitated.
Whispering Maladies - The Whisperer has improved affliction power based on total number of enemies.
Greater Heights – Heightened abilities cost less mana for each extra cast.
Kinetic Control – The Kinetic gains kinetic bonuses from own physical damage.
Brainburning Strikes – Whenever the Amnesiac attacks an enemy with mana burn, she triggers that affliction on the target.
Lingering Patterns - Patterns remain active for a period after channeling starts.
Double Divination – The Diviner can maintain two divination effects at a time.
Haunted Spells - Spells have increased effect on low mana targets.
Morbid Imagination – The Mindbleeder has increased illusory power the closer she is to death, based on the level of this skill.
Personal Time – The Chronomancer benefits when either slowed or hasted, with enchantments lasting longer while slower and afflictions fading quicker when hasted.
Broken Will – The Psychic lowers possession resistance and ignore possession by a percentage based on this skill level.
Double Defense Procs – Whenever a defense proc or runes triggers on the unit, it has a chance to trigger twice.
Know Your Master – Companions will not attack the Cabalist, and have a chance not to attack other party members.
Prismatic Magic – The Sage has a chance to create a random prism when this proc triggers.

Share in Consumption – Whenever a drain ability benefits an ally, the Cultist gets a portion of the effect based on this skill level.
Whirlwind Targeting – The modified skill has a chance to target all enemies adjacent to the original target.
Personal Effigy – The Effigist gains increased magic damage for each damage affliction present on her.
Chill to Frost - Whenever an enemy would be slowed enemy is slowed again, it is instead incapacitated.

Elemental Momentum — Each time the Elementalist uses an ability with a different element than the previous elemental ability, she gains a stacking bonus to cast speed and reduced mana cost. The stack resets to zero when she repeats an element from her current set.

Water Mastery – Water spells cost less mana and cast quicker.
Earth Mastery – Earth spells cost less mana and cast quicker.
Air Mastery – Air spells cost less mana and cast quicker.
Fire Mastery – Fire spells cost less mana and cast quicker.

Mana Disparity — Increases magic power based on the difference between the target's current mana and the Solomancer's current mana. Checked before the ability's mana cost is spent.
Reflected Counterspell — Prepared ability that counters an enemy spell and deals magic damage to the caster and random enemies based on the countered spell's mana cost.

Agnostic Afflictions – The Hedgemage ignores the opposing element penalty for vulnerability and exposure effects she applies. These effects retain full value even against resistances that would normally reduce them, as if the element were neutral.

An early-action specialist who seizes the opening of battle with scouted abilities that can only be used as the first action of a wave, then transform into a lesser related ability afterward. He builds aim quickly, attacks enemies at full health for bonus damage, and is difficult to eliminate before he gets to act.

Quick and affordable support built around lucky manipulation and regeneration. Generates divinity through hexes, purges, and blessings, then spends it on Benedictions — powerful single-target heals enhanced by current divinity, with overheal effects that range from possession to damage to speed depending on the type used.

A dodge-focused rebuild Rogue who invites attacks, turns misses into advantage, and uses reliable abilities that refund their costs on failure. He thrives in the open and under illumination, unlike most Rogues who prefer the shadows.

High-variance air specialist built around storm damage and stun pressure. She thrives on randomness — chaining lightning across the grid, forking attacks into splits, and stacking storm hits to overwhelm enemies — with the highest individual damage ceiling in the class when lucky damage and maximum damage align.

A prepared-resource specialist who enters battle with concoctions already brewed and ready to use without cost or preparation. She leans into healing, poison, and resurrection, and her premade system lets her open waves with full-power abilities immediately. Her capstone Premade Reserves deepens this advantage, making her the Teknixian most oriented toward sustained party management.

A sanity-sacrificing chaos mage who deliberately accumulates illusory damage on herself to unlock her most powerful abilities. She cannot be killed by her own madness — but when it expires, it becomes very real, making resource management a matter of survival.

A denial specialist who erodes the enemy's ability to function. She burns through mana, forces enemies into basic attacks, and makes them forget what they were doing. She also carries an unexpected compassionate edge, helping allies forget their wounds.

A spiritual warrior who infuses her companion with procs before it acts and rides a summoned Spirit Beast into mounted combat. She synchronizes her actions with her creature through a shared spiritual bond, raising fallen companions and granting her allies the will to survive past death.

Anti-attunement specialist who grows stronger the more completely she clears her elemental slate. She is the only wizard whose peak performance comes after spending conflux rather than before it, with her most powerful abilities gating behind having no attunements and her conflux damage rewarding precise elemental power investment over breadth.

A trap-setter and accumulator who builds up power before releasing it. Her accumulation abilities charge on first use and discharge on second, rewarding patience with amplified outputs. She also controls the detonation chain — recovering, redirecting, and shielding through it — and provides elemental shields to allies via Teknos Shielding.

A disciplined dragon form purist who draws power from maintaining a state of perfect purity. His most powerful abilities — Fist of Purity, Double Purity, Whirlwind Purity — require being completely unafflicted, while his Condition Fortress capstone makes him progressively harder to afflict as conditions accumulate. He manages corruption, stuns enemies with dragon-powered strikes, and uses focus as both a resource and a defensive tool.

A single-target executioner who signs contracts against chosen enemies, gaining combat bonuses while pursuing them and earning powerful fulfillment rewards when he personally lands the killing blow. Five contract types let the player tailor each hunt to the situation.

A critical-hit amplifier who builds toward celestial thresholds across multiple turns, generating mana, quickening herself, and purging afflictions with each enemy she crits. She wields the full elemental spectrum through a stellar lens, with her lucky damage toolkit turning probability itself into a weapon.

Earth-focused sustain specialist who stacks litany effects on allies and enemies for escalating pressure. Juggles short-duration stacking conditions that demand constant reapplication — letting them expire collapses the investment. Extended Cuts rewards commitment by progressively raising duration ceilings the more a condition is refreshed.

A quick ranged harasser who opens battle at a distance before pivoting to a more dangerous close-quarters fighter when his allies fall. He carries desperation abilities that only activate when he stands alone, rewarding survival over coordinated play.

The apex predator and most complex of the Barbarian subclasses. She cycles between four exclusive beast forms, scales overkill into team-wide debuffs, and generates Anguish from damage dealt to any ally — turning chaotic encounters into fuel. Final Wrath guarantees her death when it ends, making every use of it the last decision she makes.

The chaos amplifier of the family, built around Exertion abilities that generate Anguish from repeated misses and spread destruction through Contagious Temper. She leans fully into the Berserk condition, turning random targeting from a liability into an engine, with the Panic pair offering a rare moment of choice between embracing or escaping the disorder.

A dark necromancer who builds zombie companions from killed and afflicted enemies, using Juju Curse to turn her entire malediction toolkit into a zombie pipeline. Corpse Pile makes each death — enemy or companion — strengthen her current zombie, turning attrition into escalating companion power.

A high-risk area damage dealer whose bomb abilities hit allies and enemies identically with no discount. She layers countdowns on enemies and manages the self-threat they create using Accept Explosion, Accept Mass Explosion, Gift Bomb, and Transfer Countdown. Explosion Imminent and Kinetic Protection let her mitigate her own friendly fire. The higher the aim output, the harder the landing.

A capture-specialist who places bounty afflictions on enemies as minor actions during combat, with those bounties triggering beneficial effects when the marked enemy dies. He can stun and incapacitate targets to take them alive, gaining increasing payoffs the more bounties he has active when enemies fall.

A ranged gambler who wagers advantage and mana on battlefield conditions, collecting larger payoffs when those conditions are met. A good run leaves him flush; a bad one leaves him empty, making risk tolerance the central skill of his playstyle.

The patient tank of the Barbarian family. A slower, higher-endurance variant who defers self-damage costs to the next turn through Consequences, generating Anguish immediately while controlling when the pain lands — or redirecting it to enemies entirely with Share Consequence.

An ambush specialist who hits hardest against undamaged enemies and strips buffs from those who have fought back. He can artificially recreate full-health windows late in battle by corrupting enemy maximum health, keeping his ambush toolkit relevant throughout.

A self-sustaining predator who stays hurt to stay fed. Her healing threshold mechanic unlocks powerful abilities as applicable healing accumulates, rewarding healers who time large heals over constant top-offs, while life drain and kill-reaction heals give her independence when the support is occupied elsewhere.

A spread-influence subclass who bends time itself to delay, rush, and disorient the battlefield. She punishes fast enemies, accelerates allies, and becomes more efficient the more she leans into her hasted or slowed states. Supreme Chronomancy is one of the most powerful single abilities in the psychic tree.

Frontline healer built for endangered allies and active combat. Vitality heals grant temporary bonuses that persist until the target takes damage, and a War Domain that generates from any ally's critical hits rewards pairing him with damage-heavy parties. Perilous Divinity marks low-health targets for stronger healing while generating divinity.

A summoner who fights in concert with her conjured allies, using their mana reserves to amplify her own attacks. She manifests spectral weapons for any ally and directs her companion with precision, growing stronger the more she and her creature act as one.

A heavy crossbow specialist who attacks more slowly than other archers but deals more damage per shot with greater penetration. He is more defensive than most archer subclasses, reacting to enemy attacks against him rather than purely pressing offense, and can fortify and reload quickly between shots.

A team-oriented controller who drains stats from maledicted enemies and redistributes them to allies. She weaponizes possession and hexes for direct control while her Malign drain suite debilitates entire maledicted groups — and Share in Consumption ensures no drain benefit passes through her hands without leaving something behind.

A dualwield melee brawler who stacks bleed on enemies through relentless two-weapon exchanges and can grant himself intangibility to press the offense without interruption. His advantage generation rewards staying in the fight and bleeding targets dry.

A dual-wielding speed specialist whose defining abilities trigger on the second strike of a sequence, becoming more powerful the sooner that second hit follows the first. Speed Stance generates expertise from quicken effects, and she builds momentum and haste through attacks to fuel an escalating flurry of blows.

The armor-stripping heavyweight, built to cross the massive damage threshold and trigger cascading effects that tear down enemy defenses for the whole team. Destruction Wrath amplifies weakness power and defense reduction, but ends in forsaken and strips all enchantments — making dedicated buffers a liability rather than an asset.

The most offensively oriented bard subclass, specializing in life drain, culling, and damage-focused dischords rather than traditional support. He turns the song mechanic toward attrition and erasure — draining life, finishing weakened enemies, and using death itself as an element of his performance. Cacophony abilities reward the whole team's investment in debuffing, making him most dangerous in coordinated groups.

Affliction-resistant purge specialist who turns enemy pressure into elemental retaliation. Elemental purges double as generators and resistance enhancers scaled to current divinity, and a Protection Domain that rewards affliction resistance creates a feedback loop where enemy affliction pressure fuels his own power.

Conductor-style support who grants allies free attacks through Entourage abilities, drawing enemy aggression onto protected performers. Provokes and taunts redirect incoming damage to allies who are simultaneously shielded, dodging, or enduring. Dedicated Entourage extends every provoke granted, making each protected performer absorb more before attention shifts.

An information broker and countdown specialist who fights the future rather than the present. Her divinations expose enemy weaknesses and upcoming actions, letting the whole party respond intelligently, while her countdown abilities punish enemies for the passage of time itself.

An immovable defensive combatant who weaponizes his durability offensively. Unmovable Stance generates expertise from movement effects targeting him, and Advanced Unmovable Stance reflects delays back at enemies, turning every attempt to slow him into a punishment for the attacker.

Elemental support and disruption specialist who grants deity-named favors to allies, healing them and loading them with elemental damage adds. Simultaneously harasses enemies with water and air magic, knockdowns, and delays. Favor of the Drum doubles every favor with a free untyped add, making his allies' attacks substantially more dangerous.

A chaotic form-shifting brawler who embraces randomness and prone states as sources of power rather than liability. He shifts forms rapidly to build Fluid Punch damage, reach Ultimate Punch thresholds, and trigger Chakra Ascension — while deliberately falling prone to counter from the ground and punish enemies with Misplaced Retribution. His unpredictability is his greatest defense, with low accuracy offset by high dodge and a tendency to accidentally hit exactly the wrong person at exactly the right time.

A one-handed sword specialist who excels at counter attacks and is almost impossible to disarm or knock down. Counter Stance generates expertise whenever she counters, and her kit is built around parries and ripostes — parrying an attack, then immediately punishing the attacker with a follow-up strike.

A methodical earth-element controller who applies permanent unending afflictions that reserve her mana until enemies die or are purged. She trades mana flexibility for devastating long-term debilitation, and Mana From Dust recycles her investment when corruption finishes the job.

The most aggressive Witch subclass, stacking damage afflictions on targets to fuel piercing effigy attacks that cut through resistance. Flammability turns every fire hit into compounding bleeds, and Personal Effigy rewards taking damage herself — making her a high-risk attacker who burns hotter the more punishment she absorbs.

All-elements generalist with companion support and momentum-driven efficiency. She cycles through every element in sequence to build stacking cast speed and mana bonuses, summons earth and water elementals, and infuses allies with elemental damage adds — the most versatile and accessible wizard subclass.

An ally-empowerment specialist who assigns persistent assistant enchantments to party members. Each assistant type triggers a different proc when the assigned ally attacks — shields, heals, traps, bonus attacks, or quickening — and Activate Assistant can fire all procs simultaneously. She also fields the Shield Guardian, a fixed-behavior healing companion with no ammo interaction, and Minefield Assistant turns any attacker into a trap-seeding machine.

Light-magic specialist with exclusive access to intangible enemies and strong mana drain. Most abilities gain additional effects against incorporeal targets, and an Exorcism Domain that generates divinity proportional to total enemy mana spent rewards fighting caster-heavy encounters where the domain becomes a powerful self-sustaining engine.

A companion-focused archer whose pet falcon harries targets and enables abilities that either work better in the falcon's presence or require it outright. He uses the falcon to set up aim, distract enemies, and coordinate strikes — making his companion an active offensive asset rather than a passive attendant.

An extraordinarily accurate fighter who specializes in pinpoint attacks that can activate additional conditions at high enough values. Pinpoint Stance generates expertise from hit rolls beyond what is needed to connect, and her kit rewards fighting alone — with Alone Damage and Alone Defense passives that keep her effective as the last fighter standing.

Precise and fast, with a discipline that belies her name. Purity abilities amplify with each use but cancel on specific failure conditions, demanding focused play to maintain multiple stacks simultaneously. She grows faster as she takes damage and reaches peak power when Wrath and Berserk combine.

Defensive earth specialist who protects allies while grinding down enemy defenses. She builds damage shields, roots enemies in place, and applies layered weaknesses — her conflux abilities uniquely favor the whole party by granting elemental retaliations and stacking debuffs across every stat.

A flashy, risk-taking fighter who uses gambit abilities that either succeed spectacularly or backfire against her. Critical Stance generates expertise on critical hits, and her gambits deal high damage or critical effects at a cost — such as becoming prone on a miss or inviting counter attacks — rewarding aggressive play with chain weapons.

A pure ranged damage dealer built around called shots and burst ammo expenditure. Called shots are prepared as a minor action, name a target, and add powerful debuff effects — disarm, stun, heartstrike, slow, or delay — to the first attack used against that target on the following turn. Full Clip and Oblivion Shot are her all-in damage options. High Noon and Showdown both guarantee a counter-attack against her, rewarding Take Cover setups.

A corruption and bleed specialist who wraps her worst afflictions in criterion shells that resist purging until they deal their full damage. Expiration Surge turns every naturally expiring condition into mana, rewarding patience and long-duration stacking — Plague Cauldron's exponential corruption release is her most catastrophic payoff for waiting.

A ghost-touched subclass who exploits enemies at their weakest — specifically when their mana runs dry. She drains, haunts, and possesses with impunity against vulnerable targets, and can become intangible herself to frighten and evade. Death Knell makes her the safest handler of deep influence.

Pure restoration specialist with the mana economy to sustain heavy healing across a long battle. His cures carry addenda that scale with heal value, turning strong heals into purges, quickens, or damage adds. A Life Domain running on overheal generation lets him convert aggressive healing directly into sustained divinity.

A chaotic generalist who trades reliability for volume, deploying cheap bewitch afflictions against maledicted enemies at reduced action cost. Agnostic Afflictions removes elemental opposition penalties on vulnerability and exposure, letting her stack conditions freely regardless of enemy resistances — chaos as a feature, not a flaw.

A distance fighter who uses momentum to enhance his arrows and can penetrate armor more effectively the further away his target is. He tracks a specific enemy type, gaining bonuses against others of the same kind as his primary aim target and hitting harder the longer he sustains focus.

Control-focused water specialist with the deepest incapacitation toolkit in the class. She freezes, slows, and delays entire battlefields, with her most powerful conflux ability scaling both the number of targets incapacitated and how hard they are to wake based on how many elements she has charged.

A pattern-weaver who controls the entire battlefield through sustained channeled effects. She locks enemies into states of blindness, stun, or vulnerability for as long as she can keep her focus. Patient and methodical, she rewards players who plan their turns carefully.

Reactive counterspell specialist who punishes enemy spellcasting while sustaining channeled damage. She runs a suite of prepared counterspells that can chain indefinitely, drains mana from enemies, and uses Conflux Channeling to chain successive elemental damage sequences — the only wizard subclass that gets stronger the more the enemy commits to magic.

A burst-damage specialist who cycles through hidden states to deliver devastating arrival attacks. Each time he loses hidden — whether by choice or enemy action — he unleashes a different arrival ability covering area damage, flanking, stunning, or penetrating strikes. Mantis focused and initiative-driven, his Exposed Momentum capstone ensures every exposure accelerates his next turn.

A patient striker who builds power by holding his form and releases it explosively on transition. His unleash mechanic rewards stillness — the longer he stays in a single form, the more devastating the eventual change. He has no form preference, making him the most flexible of the monk subclasses and a strong foundation for learning the chakra system.

Chaos-specialist who floods enemies with random afflictions, unpredictable conditions, and misdirected attacks. No formal mechanic — the unpredictability is the design. Best used to overwhelm enemy resistances and create openings for allies, with a capstone that turns his own misfortune into tempo.

A spread-oriented damage dealer who turns punishment into power. Her kinetic abilities charge between turns based on physical damage she absorbs, making her uniquely dangerous when enemies focus on her. She favors broad pressure and area control over single-target dominance.

A polearm and spear specialist whose Lancing Blow attacks have a chance to pierce through the primary target and hit the enemy behind them. Retaliation Stance generates expertise through retaliating, and she brings mounted abilities and column-targeting attacks that reward controlling space and threatening multiple rows at once.

Aura-and-light specialist who illuminates the battlefield to empower allies and punish enemies. Manages multiple sustained auras simultaneously while spreading illuminate to lock enemies out of hidden and set up targeted light abilities. Constant Light makes him a hard counter to all stealth-based enemy strategies, fundamentally reshaping how battles play out at Tier 25.

The apex Witch, combining covenants, curses, and mass malediction into a comprehensive affliction dominance platform. She channels malediction across entire enemy groups with Malefaction Chant, unifies damage through Sympathy, and elevates her whole party's affliction pressure through Cursed Amplification — the Witch's toolkit at its most absolute.

A dual-wield closer who grows faster and hits harder the more enemies die. Rampage scales with kills — personal kills more than team kills — making bloodlust and counter abilities the tools that keep her offense rolling between turns and feeding the escalation she depends on.

An accuracy and penetration specialist who places marks on enemies that grant his allies benefits when they attack the same targets. He is the team's force multiplier at range, making his aim target more dangerous for everyone and sharing his exceptional accuracy with those who follow his lead.

The party coordinator. Rather than dominating enemies directly, she possesses allies to direct them more efficiently and uses total influence to synchronize team timing. She rewards players who understand their whole roster and rewards smart sequencing over raw power.

A balanced-alignment caster who draws equal power from both dark and light, strongest when she resists pushing to either extreme. Her Harmony abilities detonate from center for massive effect, then push her off balance — and she spends the next turns clawing her way back.

A high-risk, high-reward glass cannon who bleeds the mind as much as the body. She deals devastating illusory damage that grows stronger the closer she is to death. Her own abilities hurt her, but the connection flows both ways — and she intends to make that cost worth it.

Crescendo-driven buffer who rewards spending small actions on allies to power up larger payoffs. Builds Crescendo stacks through move and minor buffs, then releases them through scaling heal, shield, damage, bleed, and mana abilities. Leans toward chords and positive effects, with strong regeneration support alongside his offensive Crescendo tools.

Dark magic manipulator who fights most effectively when enemies cannot see him. Avert, scorn, and hidden each provide a different path to his veiled abilities, which hit harder than normal. Elusive Rhythm turns successful misdirection into tempo, rewarding a Mountebank who keeps multiple avoidance conditions active simultaneously.

Resurrection-focused support whose most powerful abilities unlock only after an ally returns to life. Epiphany abilities turn each resurrection into a cascade of heals, buffs, mana, and free attacks. His retaliation theme gives him an offensive identity when not raising allies, and Encore ensures he can survive long enough to finish his performance.

Dark magic specialist who turns death itself into a resource. She raises skeletal companions, scales her storm damage to the body count, and runs a suite of prepared abilities that trigger automatically when enemies fall — rewarding her for battles where allies are doing the killing as much as her own.

A hidden-mastery specialist who chains haste, advantage, and free bonus attacks by maintaining concealment across multiple actions. He rewards players who have mastered the hidden economy, with insidious attacks and precise sequencing separating competent play from exceptional play.

A Thanatos-leaning controller who wraps herself and allies in retaliatory spirits, punishing enemies for every strike they land. She pairs water and air magic for freeze and delay with a cross-alignment toolkit that rewards deliberate dips into Eros.

Capstone Cleric whose Furtherance abilities scale with divinity gained during the current turn rather than total on hand. Front-loading a turn with support actions directly amplifies his payoff. A Prophecy Domain that generates divinity when countdowns fire — scaled to their duration — rewards patience and long-term planning over reactive play.

A high-commitment alignment specialist who signs powerful ongoing Pacts, each granting two bonuses at the cost of one persistent drawback. She thrives at the extremes of the alignment scale, and her Lifebond with her companion means their fates are literally intertwined — she cannot fall while it stands.

A heavy shield bearer who fights best alongside ready allies. Shield Stance generates expertise on every block, and her toolkit includes guaranteed blocks, fortification at the cost of tired, and Phalanx Power, which enhances the damage of all ready allies based on how many are still standing.

Self-infecting contagion spreader who carries disease deliberately to fuel his domain. Plague Domain generates divinity for each affliction successfully transferred from the Plague Doctor to an enemy, rewarding stacking afflictions on himself and building around affliction resistance to survive the risk. One of the most dangerous and mechanically demanding Cleric subclasses.

A kill-opportunist who triggers immediate prepared attacks the moment an enemy becomes endangered, without those poach abilities being interruptible by damage. He gains culling abilities, preferences for specific target types, and benefits from kills — a specialist at finishing weakened prey faster than anyone else can reach them.

Sleep-focused controller who worships the sleeping god and grows in power while the world slumbers. Incapacitated allies feed Rest Domain divinity generation even without the Preacher acting, turning sleep from a liability into a resource. Turns ally afflictions into advantages and punishes sleeping enemies with a focused suite of nightmare attacks.

Magically aggressive Cleric who layers blessings onto allies while maintaining his own damage shield as an offensive weapon. The Lattice ability line scales with and consumes his shield for light damage and control, Lattice Reflection punishes enemies who target it, and a Sun Domain that generates from light abilities rewards sustained Celestial offense.

A relentless single-target brawler who punishes the same enemy turn after turn through his impact mechanic. Any enemy he struck last turn becomes the target of a suite of specialized follow-up attacks covering damage, delay, disruption, and control. Lower chakra focused and strength-enhanced, he hits harder the longer he stays locked onto one target.

The pinnacle of possession mastery. She owns enemies outright, bends their will across multiple turns, and profits from every attack they make under her control. Her capstone, Broken Will, ensures that no enemy is ultimately beyond her reach.

Area fire specialist who hits everyone, repeatedly. She applies countdowns, causes wounds, and commits fully to upfront mana costs for abilities that pay off over multiple ticks — Catastrophe and Conflux Meteor reward planning several turns ahead and punish enemies who cannot interrupt her.

Pure escalating output. She accumulates damage dealt toward a threshold that briefly unlocks Brink abilities — powerful options that vanish if not taken — and can sustain Endless Wrath longer than any other subclass before the drain finally overtakes her.

A shield-and-weapon fighter who builds active defenses only to spend them all at once. Reckless abilities consume all block, dodge, and counter values for amplified attacks, rewarding players who time the exposed window around a supporting tank or use it as a finisher when consequences can't resolve.

A relic-stacking power escalator who activates multi-ability relics that grow stronger with each ammo devotion. Each devoted ammo type is locked until the relic ends — which it cannot be cancelled until max devotion — creating deep commitment costs in exchange for battlefield-wide buffs, persistent damage, companion power, or trap generation. Relic Blast and Relic Bolt scale with total ammo devoted across all active relics, making a fully stacked Reliquarian increasingly devastating the longer a wave goes on.

An initiative-focused dual-wielder who seizes the opening of every battle with maximum aggression. Dodge Stance generates expertise on dodges, and Suicide Stance trades increased offense and counter-chance for the willingness to be struck, generating expertise from taking hits and rewarding an all-or-nothing fighting style.

A slow-burn debuff-accumulator whose six concoctions apply ongoing effects while building power each clock tick, then discharge a scaled effect when the chain fires or time runs out. More ammo at placement extends the window and increases accumulated power at detonation. A Faraday sub-theme lets her wear lightning rod deliberately and redirect incoming storm damage offensively through Faraday Connection's pain link.

A chaotic support-attacker who thrives on unpredictability. Her scavenged abilities reveal their element on preparation rather than use, making her toolkit flexible but harder to plan around. She generates ammo from kills and builds belts from whatever she has on hand — a scrappy, resource-efficient subclass that rewards improvisation.

A support specialist who prepares a battery of Attendant abilities and waits for her companion to critical — triggering all of them at once in a cascade of healing, damage, and quickening. The longer she waits, the more devastating the payoff.

A trick-shot specialist whose accuracy-dependent abilities pierce through targets to hit columns behind them and have reduced hit chance but significant effects when they connect. His trick shot success rate scales with current aim relative to maximum aim, rewarding sustained focus on a single target before committing to the high-risk high-reward shots.

A companion-amplifier who fields extremely slow, powerful siege engine companions — Ballista, Battering Ram, and Catapult — and spends her own actions making them fire more frequently. Every move and minor ability in her kit serves the companion: Operate Siege Engine quickens it directly, Teamwork Operation converts party delay into companion clock advancement, and Siege Command upgrades whatever the companion would do next. Her own attacks like Amplifying Cannonshot and Earth Cannon give her meaningful damage when she steps away from the engine.

A fast, opportunistic fighter who mirrors his enemies' own strengths against them through the matching mechanic. He can temporarily adopt a target's critical stats, damage, accuracy, defense, or dodge — turning powerful enemies into their own worst nightmare. Leopard form focused and haste-driven, he excels at demolishing stunned foes and stacking bleeds through repeated Leopard Claw cycles.

A defensively self-reliant Rogue who applies aversion to make enemies ignore him, then punishes them for it. He complements aversion with scorn to layer targeting protection, generating advantage steadily from the safety of being overlooked.

A team-oriented Rogue whose power scales with how many allies are hidden alongside him. He can blanket the party in shadow, share his poisons across the team, and coordinate hidden allies into a unified striking force.

Light magic specialist with hex, justice, and a unique mana economy identity. She wants enemies casting expensive spells so her Mana Disparity bonus peaks, making her the only wizard who benefits from enemy casters. Her full-conflux Conflux Enchantment can grant the entire party six simultaneous buffs scaled to her elemental investment.

A desperation specialist whose entire toolkit unlocks at low health, becoming most powerful precisely when she should be most vulnerable. Her transformation locks in that endangered power permanently, turning near-death into a lasting combat state.

Stealth-integrated bard who supplements song management with disguises and flanking setups. Each disguise grants role-specific bonuses and can be dramatically discharged for a powerful effect at the cost of the disguise itself. Begins every battle already in disguise, giving immediate access to his full toolkit from the first action.

A shadow-fighter who generates aim from hidden status and converts high accuracy into higher damage, with a defining ability that expends all accumulated aim for a devastating single attack — but then prevents him from targeting that specific enemy for a period scaled to the aim spent.

A fortified earth specialist who turns glancing blows from a weakness into a weapon. His attacks deliberately seek glancing hits to trigger stuns, bleeds, delays, and fragility — and his Pressure Crack capstone extends this to critical hits as well. Tiger form focused and endurance-heavy, he is nearly immovable under sustained assault and punishes enemies for every attempt to pierce his defenses.

A sword-fighting parry expert whose feint abilities compel enemies to attack her, then punish them when she parries the incoming strike. Parry Stance generates expertise from each successful parry, and she chains feints into ripostes, bleeds, penetrating attacks, or mass taunts depending on which feint variant she has prepared.

The entry point for deep influence play. The Telepath specializes in illusory damage and disruption, with heightened abilities that let her translate influence investment into cascading multi-cast effects. She is subtle and methodical, chipping away at enemy defenses before they can act.

Pinnacle attunement-breadth specialist who rewards deliberate, expensive play. She wants all six elements charged simultaneously, spends them through Supreme abilities that scale with attunement count, and uses her previous turn's mana expenditure to amplify the next — the most technically demanding wizard subclass and the one with the highest ceiling.

A self-sufficient dualwield fighter who steals accuracy, speed, and senses from enemies to empower himself. He can briefly share his incoming healing and mana gain with allies, giving a team-oriented edge to an otherwise personal playstyle.

A chain-combat specialist who builds devastating sequences of air, stun, and shatter effects through careful ability ordering. Nearly every move and minor ability has a trigger condition — following a counter, a critical, a shatter, or an air attack — creating dense combo potential that rewards mechanical knowledge. Crane focused and counter-driven, his Thunder Strikes capstone ensures every stunned enemy takes bonus air damage on each hit.

A modification-based companion commander who toggles different behavioral modes to reshape her companion and her own attacks. Her four modular abilities — Modular Bomb, Modular Ray, Modular Trap, and Modular Beam — each change behavior based on which modifications are active. Flame Spewer and Lightning Tosser are ammo-sensitive companions that change element and effect based on what's loaded at summoning.

A distance-and-duration specialist who builds power over the course of a long battle through eternal buff abilities that grow without limit but become progressively more expensive to enhance. Only one can be active at a time, demanding that the player commit to a single compounding effect and protect the Toxophilite long enough for it to pay off.

A deliberate shield fighter who charges prepared abilities through sustained blocking. Each block adds power to any held ability, and multiple prepared abilities charge independently, rewarding patient setup and precise release timing over the Raider's impulsive spending.

A poison-crafting snake form specialist who generates unique toxins from his own body and bleeds. He creates poisons based on his current form through Venom Chakra, conserves and refreshes them through careful resource management, and delivers them through venomous, insidious, and backbiting strikes. Earth and dark elemental focused, he excels at sustained damage over time and attrition warfare.

A selfish corruptor who damages her own allies to fuel her offensive power, scaling with the total corruption she spreads across the battlefield. She transforms her own self-inflicted corruption into a permanent power state, and turns enemy deaths into mana through Dark Harvest.

An air-element Witch who turns malediction into a positional weapon. Her whirlwind abilities use a maledicted enemy as an anchor, striking all adjacent foes instead — rewarding grid awareness and central positioning. Bloodlust amplifies her storm attacks while Conductivity makes the entire maledicted field a lightning rod.

A commanding leader who translates her own expertise directly into team-wide benefits. Warlord's Stance generates expertise whenever any ally acts, and her Leadership abilities require a minimum expertise level and become more powerful at higher thresholds — quickening all allies, enhancing their damage, or even making their next attack unerring after she misses.

A water-element specialist who deals increased damage and effects in inverse proportion to enemy speed — making her strongest against the foes she has already slowed. Chill to Frost converts redundant slows into hard incapacitation, and Inspiring Misfortune makes her one of the strongest mana generators in the entire Witch family.

A light-element support Witch who harvests fetishes from fallen enemies and deploys them as stat-scaling ally buffs. She transfers afflictions from allies to enemies, drains life, and accumulates mana through Fetish Bag by holding fetishes in reserve — balancing the tension between deploying her toolkit and sustaining herself.

An immovable reactive combatant who weaponizes his chakra configuration to punish every enemy attack. Snake's Response reflects conditions back at attackers based on which chakras are open, with the lower chakras delivering the most devastating punishments — prone, delay, and disarm simultaneously at full configuration. He fights best when pristine, baiting attacks while armed with Reversal, Absorbed Counter, and a full suite of prepared reactions.

High-speed melee Cleric who conducts the entire party's tempo through quickening. Ascension abilities require but do not spend full divinity, creating a maintain-and-hold pattern rather than the typical spend-and-rebuild cycle. A mastery class at Tier 19 — maximizing output requires deep awareness of quicken tolerance, Ascension timing, and Fervor Domain generation simultaneously.

Bloodlust Rampage – Melee attack that has increased bloodlust value for each enemy killed in battle (Marauder)
Clobbering Rampage – Melee attack that has increased clobbering value for each enemy killed in battle (Marauder)
Clobbering Rend – Two melee attacks against a single target. Uses clobbering if both attacks hit (Marauder)
Critical Assault – Melee attack that attacks all on critical. Consumes rage (Marauder)
Double Attack – Two melee attacks that add together before comparison to defense (Marauder)
Dual Rampage – Melee attack requiring dual wielding that deals additional damage for each enemy killed in battle (Marauder)
Eviscerating Rend – Two melee attacks against a single target. Causes heartstrike if both attacks hit (Marauder)
Off-hand Preparations – Dual wield melee attack that compels target and enhances counter chance (Marauder)
Onslaught Rampage – Dual-wield melee attack that makes an additional attack on a random enemy for each enemy killed in battle (Marauder)
Vicious Tumult – Melee attack with bloodlust with increased accuracy and critical chance based on bloodlust, consumes rage (Marauder)
Wave of Bloodlust – Melee attack against all with bloodlust (Marauder)
Bloodlust Response – Melee attack with bloodlust following a block (Viking)
Continuous Turmoil – Attack, then attack all on critical (Viking)
Furious Tumult – Melee attack with bloodlust that consumes rage (Viking)
Razor Shield – Prepared melee attack with high untyped bleed. Enhanced by blocks made since preparation. (Viking)
Shield Decimation – Prepared melee attack with decimate. Enhanced by blocks made since preparation. (Viking)
Shield Smash — Prepared melee attack. Damage and clobbering value enhanced by blocks made since preparation. (Viking)
Shield Throw – Prepared melee attack against all enemies. Enhanced by blocks made since preparation. (Viking)
Shield Wall – Prepared melee attack against enemy row. Enhanced by blocks made since preparation. (Viking)
Steel Suffering – Melee attack that causes untyped bleed and defense weakness (Viking)
Taunting Axe – Melee attack with damage increased by rage that taunts enemies (Viking)
Taunting Shield – Melee attack that enhances block chance and taunts enemies (Viking)
Undertow Blow – Prepared unblockable water melee attack that delays and causes water bleed (Viking)
Violent Push – Melee attack that causes prone to enemies behind target (Viking)
Awesome Cleave – Melee attack versus single that damages all other enemies against combined defense of primary and secondary target (Vandal)
Brink of Death – Melee attack with ruthless damage. Only becomes available for one turn immediately after dealing enough damage (Vandal)
Brink of Inferno – Fire melee attack that grants fire damage add. Only becomes available for one turn immediately after dealing enough damage (Vandal)
Brink of Onslaught – Three randomly targeting melee attacks. Only becomes available for one turn immediately after dealing enough damage (Vandal)
Brink of Violence – Melee attack with backbiting. Only becomes available for one turn immediately after dealing enough damage (Vandal)
Endless Beating – Prepared melee attack. This attack stays prepared if you are raging (Vandal)
Escalating Violence – Melee attack with amplification that is always countered (Vandal)
Ferocious Spree – Melee attack with amplification that consumes increasing amounts of rage (Vandal)
Intimidating Charge – Melee attack with momentum that causes frightened, requires rage (Vandal)
Raging Cleave – Large weapon attack that strikes target enhanced by rage and adjacent enemies based on rage (Vandal)
Ruthless Strike – Ruthless melee attack requiring rage (Vandal)
Ultimate Violence – Melee attack consuming rage that deals maximum damage (Vandal)
Amplified Savagery – Melee attack with backbiting and amplification, can be used berserk (Fury)
Blood Purity – Melee attack with increasing bleed, resets if barbarian attacks the target suffering from this bleed. (Fury)
Critical Purity – Melee attack with increased critical chance and critical damage, but with reduced accuracy, resets if the barbarian misses. (Fury)
Endless Exchange – Melee attack that causes tired for self and target. Tired duration increased for target and decreased for herself based on rage (Fury)
Expeditious Strike – Melee attack that quickens the fury and that requires haste. Can be used while berserk (Fury)
Furious Drive – Melee attack that enhances speed on critical, stacking. Increased critical chance based on rage and can be used berserk (Fury)
Killing Amplification – Melee attack that provides amplification with any other ability on kill (Fury)
Quickening Purity – Melee attack with increasing quicken effect, but it reduces defense and dodge. This can be disrupted. (Fury)
Ranged Purity – Ranged attack with increasing damage, but this resets if the barbarian attacks a close enemy. (Fury)
Sacrifice Purity – Melee attack with increasing damage and backbiting, but this ends if the barbarian is healed. (Fury)
Staggering Fury – Melee storm with delay on each hit (Fury)
Storm Purity – Melee attack. Each use makes an additional random attack, each with backbite, but this ends if the same enemy is hit twice in a turn. (Fury)
Bloodlust Bite – Melee attack with bloodlust requiring rage (Cannibal)
Devour the Sleeping – Culling melee attack against incapacitated target. Heal on kill (Cannibal)
Devour Whole – Cull target enemy to heal, gain mana, and gain all enchantments on target enemy (Cannibal)
Gnashing Consumption – Melee attack that causes untyped bleed on target. Requires the Cannibal to have received enough healing (Cannibal)
Grave Hunger – Melee attack with drain requiring Cannibal to be endangered (Cannibal)
Health Stealing Bite – Melee attack with drain that also applies heal siphon to target (Cannibal)
Mana Consumption – Melee attack that drains mana from target. Requires the Cannibal to have received enough healing (Cannibal)
Maximum Satiation – Maximized melee attack requiring Cannibal has been healed enough (Cannibal)
Rabid Bite – Melee attack with untyped bleed and wound (Cannibal)
Sacrificial Consumption – Melee attack with backbiting. Requires having been healed enough (Cannibal)
Unsated Hunger – Prepared melee attack with life drain that becomes unprepared if Cannibal is healed (Cannibal)
Vampiric Bite – Melee attack with drain requiring rage (Cannibal)
Approaching Victory – Melee attack that quickens all based on overkill (Destroyer)
Cascading Critical – Melee attack that cascades to random target on critical (Destroyer)
Critical Balance – Melee attack that cannot critical, but deals additional damage based on critical damage (Destroyer)
Destroy Armor – Melee attack with shattering that causes fragile to the target (Destroyer)
Entropy Hammer – Melee attack with clobbering that deals corrupt damage (Destroyer)
Grudgebearer – Attack with defense weakness against enemy that attacked unit turn before (Destroyer)
Massive Burst – Melee attack that damages all enemies if it deals massive damage (Destroyer)
Massive Cascade – Melee attack that cascades if attack deals massive damage. This effect can repeat multiple times, but each cascade must target a different enemy (Destroyer)
Massive Corruption – Melee attack that converts damage to corrupt if it is massive damage (Destroyer)
Massive Destruction – Melee attack that lowers all enemy defense if it deals massive damage (Destroyer)
Massive Stupidity – Melee attack that disrupts and deals mana damage to all enemies if it deals massive damage (Destroyer)
Massive Suffering – Massive damage melee attack with backbiting (Destroyer)
Weapon Fracture – Melee attack with shattering that can disarm the target (Destroyer)
Animalistic Attack – Melee attack based on current animal form. Consumes rage (Beastlord)
Bull’s Rampage – Three random melee attack that cause bleed and requires rage (Beastlord)
Call Rampaging Rhino – Summons a rampaging rhino mount with trample abilities (Beastlord)
Feral Health Strike – Melee attack that heals user. Heals extra if attack kills (Beastlord)
Might Exacerbation – Melee attack that requires berserk, enhances damage but Beastlord becomes tired (Beastlord)
Raging Charge – Mounted melee attack enhanced by rage (Beastlord)
Rampant Umbrage – Melee attack that deals damage based on overkill of previous attack (Beastlord)
Rending Force – Melee attack that lowers defense of all enemies by overkill (Beastlord)
Riven Force – Melee attack that lowers damage of all enemies based on overkill (Beastlord)
Trample Underfoot – Mounted melee attack versus column. Each enemy counters the beastlord, but the beastlord generates extra rage for the damage. On a critical, enemies are knocked prone (Beastlord)
Ultimate Rage Strike – Consume all remaining rage and end rage form immediately to make massive attack (Beastlord)
Glancing Guarantee – Melee attack that deals only glancing damage (Raider)
Rage Shield – Consume rage to guarantee block against next attack. Also stuns attacker (Raider)
Reckless Haste – Gain haste based on block chance and amount. Prevents active defenses and counters for same duration (Raider)
Reckless Impact – Delay all enemies. Prevents Raider from using active defenses and counters until next turn (Raider)
Shield Clobber – Melee attack using shield with clobber (Raider)
Shield Recklessness – Melee attack following block. Prevents all active defenses until next turn (Raider)
Berserk Jab – Melee attack that requires berserk (Berserker)
Berserk Patience – Counter next attack. Requires berserk (Berserker)
Berserker Strength – Enhance damage for a period. Requires berserk (Berserker)
Contagious Temper – Berserks all allies and enhances damage for their next attack. Requires berserk, can be used berserk (Berserker)
Extra Exertion – Take damage and repeat exertion ability that missed twice. (Berserker)
Vicious Rampage – Enhance damage and speed for a period. Become fatigued when buff is lost (Berserker)
Counter Rampage – Guarantee counter against next attack. Requires enough enemies killed in battle, and enhanced for total enemies killed in battle (Marauder)
Deadly Persistence – Follows a kill with a melee attack (Marauder)
Doubled Counter – Next counter attacks with both weapons. Requires dual-wielding (Marauder)
Rage Counter – Counter next attack with damage enhanced by rage. Requires and consumes rage (Marauder)
Rampage Haste – Grants Marauder haste based on the number of enemies killed in battle (Marauder)
Rampage Hostility – Enhances damage based on number of enemies killed. Consumes rage (Marauder)
Rampage Speed – Quickens Marauder based on number of enemies killed in battle (Marauder)
Savage Shield – Melee attack with shield following block. Consumes rage (Viking)
Shield Sacrifice – Enhance block chance until next turn. Costs life. (Viking)
Shield Smash – Melee attack. Prevents blocking until next turn, based on usual block chance and block amount (Viking)
Shield of Superstition – Enhance magic resistance and lower block chance until next turn (Viking)
Shield to Shield – Prepared ability that triggers on block. Prevent target enemy from blocking for a period (Viking)
Splash Shield – Prepared ability that deals water damage to front row on next block (Viking)
